Investigate. Start by locating the executive revenue KPI in DataHub.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

tools.name: profile_column

tools.name: run_sql

tools.description: List the SQL transform files.
tools.name: list_transforms

tools.description: Read one SQL transform.
tools.name: read_transform

tools.description: Run the pipeline invariant suite on the current warehouse.
tools.name: run_checks

tools.description: Confirm a root cause with cited evidence; use this (then propose_repair) whenever the true values can be reconstructed exactly. Can be called again to revise the root cause before a repair passes. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.
tools.name: confirm_root_cause

tools.description: Escalate upstream data that is lost, missing or stale and cannot be recovered exactly. No repair is allowed afterwards. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.
tools.name: escalate_upstream

tools.description: Declare no incident, citing a baseline comparison.
tools.name: declare_no_incident

tools.description: Replace one transform's full SQL; the pipeline is rebuilt in a scratch copy and every invariant is checked.
tools.name: propose_repair

tools.description: Record the incident in DataHub on the affected dataset.
tools.name: write_back

tools.description: End the run with a final report.
tools.name: finish

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:

     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.

  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format

     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,

  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

content.text: Confirmed: clean cutover at 2026-08-07. Before that, `currency` is always populated and `currency_code` is always null. On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

content.text: Confirmed: clean cutover at 2026-08-07. Before that, `currency` is always populated and `currency_code` is always null. On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

input.summary: Exec revenue KPI (marts.exec_metric) shows revenue=NULL for 2026-08-07..09 while order_count stays normal (ev_002), and compare_to_baseline shows no deviation prior to that gap (ev_003). Lineage traces exec_metric -> marts.fct_revenue -> staging.stg_orders/stg_fx_rates -> raw.raw_orders/raw.raw_fx_rates (ev_005). raw.raw_fx_rates is fully up to date through 08-09 with no gaps (ev_008, ev_009), ruling out FX staleness. Root cause is in raw.raw_orders: the upstream payments-platform contract silently renamed the `currency` field to `currency_code` starting exactly at 2026-08-07 00:00:00 (ev_020: before cutover 24977 rows all have currency populated & currency_code null; after cutover 793 rows all have currency null & currency_code populated), coinciding with a new payment_processor value 'cloudpay_v2' (ev_017, ev_016). The two columns are mutually exclusive across all history (ev_021, ev_022), confirming a clean rename rather than a data quality issue. staging.stg_orders (ev_010) only selects the old `currency` column, so every order since 08-07 gets currency=NULL, which then fails the join to staging.stg_fx_rates (f.currency = o.currency) in fct_revenue.sql (ev_007), nulling out revenue_usd/aov_usd for all affected days while COUNT(*) (order_count) is unaffected -- exactly matching the observed symptom.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o

On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

content.text: Confirmed: clean cutover at 2026-08-07. Before that, `currency` is always populated and `currency_code` is always null. On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

content.text: Both columns are mutually exclusive across the full history — a clean rename, not overlapping data. This is deterministically recoverable: `currency_code` holds exactly the values `currency` used to hold, just under a new name. I'll fix `stg_orders.sql` to coalesce both columns.

input.summary: Exec revenue KPI (marts.exec_metric) shows revenue=NULL for 2026-08-07..09 while order_count stays normal (ev_002), and compare_to_baseline shows no deviation prior to that gap (ev_003). Lineage traces exec_metric -> marts.fct_revenue -> staging.stg_orders/stg_fx_rates -> raw.raw_orders/raw.raw_fx_rates (ev_005). raw.raw_fx_rates is fully up to date through 08-09 with no gaps (ev_008, ev_009), ruling out FX staleness. Root cause is in raw.raw_orders: the upstream payments-platform contract silently renamed the `currency` field to `currency_code` starting exactly at 2026-08-07 00:00:00 (ev_020: before cutover 24977 rows all have currency populated & currency_code null; after cutover 793 rows all have currency null & currency_code populated), coinciding with a new payment_processor value 'cloudpay_v2' (ev_017, ev_016). The two columns are mutually exclusive across all history (ev_021, ev_022), confirming a clean rename rather than a data quality issue. staging.stg_orders (ev_010) only selects the old `currency` column, so every order since 08-07 gets currency=NULL, which then fails the join to staging.stg_fx_rates (f.currency = o.currency) in fct_revenue.sql (ev_007), nulling out revenue_usd/aov_usd for all affected days while COUNT(*) (order_count) is unaffected -- exactly matching the observed symptom.

content.text: Now I'll patch `stg_orders.sql` to coalesce the renamed column, scoped so historical rows (which already have `currency` populated) are unaffected.

input.new_sql:
-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    COALESCE(currency, currency_code) AS currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

content.text: Confirmed: clean cutover at 2026-08-07. Before that, `currency` is always populated and `currency_code` is always null. On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

The two columns are mutually exclusive across all history (ev_021, ev_022), confirming a clean rename rather than a data quality issue. staging.stg_orders (ev_010) only selects the old `currency` column, so every order since 08-07 gets currency=NULL, which then fails the join to staging.stg_fx_rates (f.currency = o.currency) in fct_revenue.sql (ev_007), nulling out revenue_usd/aov_usd for all affected days while COUNT(*) (order_count) is unaffected -- exactly matching the observed symptom.

{"evidence_id": "ev_006", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

content.text: Confirmed: clean cutover at 2026-08-07. Before that, `currency` is always populated and `currency_code` is always null. On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

Root cause is in raw.raw_orders: the upstream payments-platform contract silently renamed the `currency` field to `currency_code` starting exactly at 2026-08-07 00:00:00 (ev_020: before cutover 24977 rows all have currency populated & currency_code null; after cutover 793 rows all have currency null & currency_code populated), coinciding with a new payment_processor value 'cloudpay_v2' (ev_017, ev_016). The two columns are mutually exclusive across all history (ev_021, ev_022), confirming a clean rename rather than a data quality issue. staging.stg_orders (ev_010) only selects the old `currency` column, so every order since 08-07 gets currency=NULL, which then fails the join to staging.stg_fx_rates (f.currency = o.currency) in fct_revenue.sql (ev_007), nulling out revenue_usd/aov_usd for all affected days while COUNT(*) (order_count) is unaffected -- exactly matching the observed symptom.

content.text: Now I'll patch `stg_orders.sql` to coalesce the renamed column, scoped so historical rows (which already have `currency` populated) are unaffected.

-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    COALESCE(currency, currency_code) AS currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

    customer_id,

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:

     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream

   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(rate_day AS DATE) AS rate_day,
        currency,
        CAST(usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate
    FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(t.d AS DATE) AS day, c.currency
    FROM range(DATE '2026-05-12', DATE '2026-08-10', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM rates) AS c
)
SELECT
    s.day AS rate_day,
    s.currency,
    CASE WHEN s.day - r.rate_day <= 2 THEN r.usd_rate END AS usd_rate,
    r.rate_day AS source_rate_day
FROM spine AS s
ASOF LEFT JOIN rates AS r
    ON s.currency = r.currency AND s.day >= r.rate_day;
"}

On/after 2026-08-07, it's the reverse — the upstream source (payments platform) renamed/moved the field to `currency_code` for all processors (coinciding with the new `cloudpay_v2` processor rollout), but `staging.stg_orders` still only reads the old `currency` column, so it silently nulls out for every order in that window. That breaks the currency join in `fct_revenue` (NULL never matches `stg_fx_rates.currency`), zeroing out `revenue_usd`/`aov_usd` while `order_count` stays intact — exactly matching the KPI symptom (revenue null the last 3 days, order counts normal).

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

input.report:
INCIDENT: Exec revenue KPI drop (marts.exec_metric)

SYMPTOM: revenue_usd and aov_median_usd went NULL for 2026-08-07, 08-08, 08-09 while order_count stayed in the normal range (222-297/day baseline). compare_to_baseline confirmed no deviation in the 11 days prior to the gap (ratios = 1.0), so this was a sudden-onset break, not a gradual demand decline.

LINEAGE: marts.exec_metric <- marts.fct_revenue <- staging.stg_orders / staging.stg_customers / staging.stg_fx_rates <- raw.raw_orders / raw.raw_customers / raw.raw_fx_rates (DataHub lineage, ev_005).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, asset=raw.raw_orders, field=currency): The upstream payments-platform source silently renamed the `currency` column to `currency_code` for all orders starting exactly 2026-08-07 00:00:00 UTC, coinciding with the rollout of a new payment_processor value 'cloudpay_v2'. Before the cutover, 24,977 rows had `currency` populated and `currency_code` NULL; after the cutover, all 793 rows had `currency` NULL and `currency_code` populated -- a clean rename, not a data-quality/overlap issue (ev_016, ev_017, ev_020, ev_021, ev_022). raw.raw_fx_rates was checked and found fully fresh/complete through 08-09 (ev_008, ev_009), ruling out FX staleness as the cause.

staging.stg_orders only selected the legacy `currency` column (ev_010), so every order since the cutover carried currency=NULL downstream. marts.fct_revenue joins stg_orders to stg_fx_rates ON currency (ev_007); a NULL never matches, so revenue_usd/aov_usd/aov_median_usd computed to NULL for every affected day while order_count (a plain COUNT(*)) was unaffected -- exactly matching the observed KPI symptom.

CLASSIFICATION: Recoverable exactly. The true currency values are fully reconstructable via COALESCE(currency, currency_code) because the two columns are strictly mutually exclusive across all history.

REPAIR: Patched staging/stg_orders.sql to compute currency as COALESCE(currency, currency_code). This is a minimal, scoped change (single column expression) that does not rewrite any historical values (pre-cutover rows already had `currency` populated, so COALESCE is a no-op for them). Verified via propose_repair: pipeline rebuilt in scratch copy, full invariant suite passed.

UPSTREAM CONTRACT VIOLATION: raw.raw_orders' owning team (payments platform / Jordan Lee) changed the documented contract (payments-platform v1.3, "one row per order attempt") by renaming `currency` -> `currency_code` without notice. This should be fixed/versioned properly upstream; we've patched around it downstream for now. Recorded in DataHub via write_back.

ACTIONS TAKEN: confirm_root_cause -> propose_repair (verified) -> write_back -> finish.
